body:
Global crypto market cap sits at $2.95T after a -2.44% drawdown over the past 24 hours, yet the mood on the desk reads more cautious consolidation than outright fear. The Fear and Greed index actually ticked higher, from 70 yesterday to 73 today, suggesting retail sentiment remains stubbornly in Greed territory even as aggregate valuations compress. Total 24-hour volume across the market came in at $81.6B, a figure that doesn't scream panic selling but equally doesn't suggest conviction buying. BTC dominance at 58.8% and ETH dominance at 11.2% tell the deeper story: capital is hugging the largest asset in the space and not venturing far down the risk curve, which is the right instinct given how choppy the mid-cap and small-cap layers are trading.

Bitcoin is printing $86,403 at time of writing, essentially flat on a 24-hour basis at +0.10% and barely moving on the hour at -0.05%. The 7-day picture is more constructive at +2.22%, confirming that BTC has been grinding higher in a controlled fashion rather than spiking. Volume at $28.08B is healthy but not exuberant. The key story here is the psychological and technical significance of the $85,000-$87,000 band — BTC has now spent multiple sessions in this corridor, and a clean daily close above $87,000 would be the first meaningful signal that the next leg higher is loading. Conversely, any intraday push below $84,000 on elevated volume would flip the near-term bias back to range-bound caution.

Ethereum at $2,717.18 is underperforming its larger sibling, down -0.16% on the day and -0.61% on the week, which reinforces the BTC-dominance narrative. The divergence is worth flagging: while BTC has added +2.22% over 7 days, ETH has quietly leaked lower, and with $11.13B in 24-hour volume the selling pressure is not trivial. Among the tracked altcoin set, AVAX is the standout mover at +3.86% on the day, trading at $11.4, though the weekly chart still shows -2.84% so today reads more like a dead-cat bounce than a trend reversal. ADA at $0.275943 is the week's quiet winner at +9.22% over 7 days, with a modest +0.53% today sustaining the move. On the other side of the ledger, LINK is the name to watch for pain: -8.70% on the week and -0.42% today at $14.02, with only $0.3B in volume suggesting there's no aggressive buying interest stepping in. UNI at $8.9 dropped -1.53% in 24 hours and is off -3.36% on the week, consistent with continued pressure on DeFi-adjacent tokens.

The macro backdrop is the dominant variable and it is sending mixed signals. A CoinDesk headline flags that the VIX of bonds is rising while bitcoin and equities have not yet priced in the stress, which is precisely the kind of dislocation that tends to resolve sharply and not gently. Oil prices and bond yields are reportedly retreating today, providing some temporary relief, but the bond volatility signal is not something to dismiss. Raoul Pal's comment, picked up by Cointelegraph, that capital is starting to rotate back to crypto from AI is an interesting qualitative data point that aligns with the marginal BTC strength, though one quote does not make a rotation. On the regulatory front, OKX raising fresh capital at a $25B valuation per Cointelegraph and Paxos launching its $3B USDG stablecoin on Arbitrum are both constructive structural signals — institutional infrastructure is being built out regardless of short-term price noise, and Arbitrum's entry into the Global Dollar stablecoin consortium adds another real-world utility layer to that ecosystem.

The next 48 to 72 hours hinge on a few specific catalysts. Bond market volatility is the primary macro risk — if yields reverse the retreat and push higher again, risk assets broadly will feel it and crypto will not be immune despite the Greed reading on sentiment. Watch whether BTC can hold above $86,000 on any intraday dips; a failure to do so opens the door to a retest of $84,000 and potentially lower. AVAX needs to confirm today's +3.86% move with follow-through volume or it fades back into its weekly downtrend. LINK at $14.02 is the clearest technical casualty right now and the question is whether the -8.70% weekly loss attracts bargain hunters or accelerates further. The stablecoin news around USDG and Arbitrum is worth monitoring for on-chain flow effects over the coming week. Any clarity on the US regulatory framework — flagged by Cointelegraph as needing to survive the next election cycle — would be a meaningful sentiment catalyst in either direction, and the market is currently trading as though that uncertainty is a background hum rather than an active risk.
